title: File path traversal
summary: Prove a path parameter escapes its intended directory and returns a test-owned out-of-directory file. An error message or an in-directory file is not proof.
steps: Locate an observed file/path/download/template parameter and establish the normal file response as a baseline.
Change only that parameter to a predictable, test-owned out-of-directory target (../ or encoded ../ to a benign app-owned file) and compare with an invalid-path control.
Prefer a single benign proof file; do not read unrelated or sensitive system files beyond that one demonstration.
If filtered, try one normalization/encoding layer (%2e%2e, ....//, an absolute path) — one variable at a time, no payload spray.
On PASS: a response whose content comes from outside the intended directory, with the exact parameter and request evidence.
KILL if only error text or an in-directory file is returned, or the path is canonicalized/allowlisted.
pass_signals: A test-owned out-of-directory file is returned for a changed path parameter
kill_signals: Only error text or an in-directory file is returned
The path is canonicalized or allowlisted
